summary: The Office of the Ohio Consumers' Counsel asks for rehearing of FERC's September 29, 2026 order accepting PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement, challenging the $555/MW-day offer cap, pay-as-bid clearing, the 20% shortage penalty and cost allocation to consumers rather than data center loads.
ask: Direct PJM to set a lower offer cap, adopt single-price clearing, replace the 20% shortage penalty, and design an RBP that allocates costs to the large loads causing the need.

points.point: OCC says the accepted RBP design does not match concurrences by Commissioners LaCerte and See that new load, not existing customers, should bear its costs.
points.quote: Existing customers should not be left paying costs attributable to new demand.

points.point: The order accepted a one-time procurement of 6,831 MW and postponed the auction five months to February 28, 2027.
points.quote: it postponed that auction for five months, until February 28, 2027.

points.point: OCC lists the paper hearing topics FERC set: zonal cost allocation, muni and co-op opt-outs, TO exit fees and LSE collateral.
points.quote: set these issues for further paper hearings and additional comments

points.point: OCC says the $555/MW-day cap and pay-as-bid clearing lack record support and do not mitigate seller market power.
points.quote: There is no evidence in the record to support this offer cap, and there is no evidence to support the pay-as-bid clearing mechanism design.

points.point: It says the cap is more than $200/MW-day above the collared cap in the 2028/2029 base residual auction.
points.quote: more than $200/MW-day higher than the current collared price cap applied in the 2028/2029 RPM base residual auction.

points.point: OCC says the 20% shortage penalty is far below RPM's non-performance penalty and shortfall charges are limited to three years against a 15-year commitment.
points.quote: FERC accepted a proposal to limit the proposed shortage penalty to only 1/5th of the capacity sell offer

points.point: It says costs should fall on data centers and FERC ignored a claimed $23.1 billion cost shift from the past three auctions.
points.quote: data center demand increased capacity costs to other PJM customers by approximately $23.1 billion

points.point: OCC's prayer asks FERC to lower the cap, adopt single clearing price, reject the 20% penalty and allocate RBP costs to cost causers.
points.quote: directing PJM to set a lower market seller offer cap for the RBP auction consistent with protests filed by OCC and others on this issue

throughLine.text: Rehearing in PJM's backstop procurement docket ER26-3380, the capacity-adequacy track running beside E-7's request that PJM report how it will ensure generation for large loads.
